findings.title: Value shifts from visible stock to durable good action
findings.claim: The focus comparison shifts the measure of value from visible wealth and offspring as adornment toward good actions that remain and receive better return with the Lord.
findings.mechanism: The b-q-y carriers supply persistence and residue, while the x-y-r carrier supplies the positive value being compared; the nearby garden loss, retained record, and parallel reward-return conclusions activate the contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish what looks valuable now from what the focus presents as a better lasting measure.
findings.containment: This is a comparative value shift, not a rejection of family or lawful wealth and not a claim that every surviving worldly asset is inherently good.

epistemic.reason: The candidate is trusted and supplies exact focus branch and anchor rows; the broader relational synthesis remains qualified because the packet's connection records are supporting parallels rather than a full proof of one causal model.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şey yok olmaz; varlığı veya içinde bulunduğu durum sürer.
branch_activations.carrier: The b-q-y carrier names what remains after the garden's visible supports collapse.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The nearby garden loss and the ordered 18:45 and 18:49 records supply loss and retained-account pressure.
branch_activations.activation: The survival facet is activated as a contrast between adornment that disperses and a good remainder that persists.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Good action is evaluated as what remains after worldly display loses its support.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not make every surviving worldly asset good or claim that the packet proves a single mechanical afterlife process.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir bütünün bir bölümü gider veya kullanılır; geride kalan bölüm sonuç olarak bulunmaya devam eder.
branch_activations.carrier: The b-q-y carrier can name the residue left when visible possession and support are stripped away.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The loss of the garden and the ordered contrast between vegetation and retained deeds supply the residue frame.
branch_activations.activation: The residue facet is activated in the movement from transient adornment to what remains available for account.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The lasting good is read as a remainder rather than as another form of visible stock.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not identify the remainder with a financial balance or reduce all good work to a remainder metaphor.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The 18:44 and 19:76 parallels join good with better reward and final return in the Lord's presence.
branch_activations.activation: The positive-value facet is activated as the focus's criterion for what outlasts worldly display.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Good is not merely another possession; it is the positive value by which the lasting alternative is judged.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation preserves the broad good-value sense and does not force every x-y-r occurrence into a single technical meaning.

findings.title: Good as a durable beneficial relation
findings.claim: The focus's good can also be perceived as a beneficial relation that outlasts visible stock and reaches another recipient across time, so wealth and offspring are not the sole carriers of benefit.
findings.mechanism: The x-y-r carrier is read through the legacy activation's explicit relation between soundness and benefit to children, with the garden-loss sequence supplying the contrast against visible stock.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the focus does not simply replace wealth with another object, but relocates benefit into a durable relation and its consequences.
findings.containment: This remains an attributed legacy reading: 18:82 is supplied as a textual pointer in the support record, not as a fully traced focus activation, and no general claim about inherited virtue is made.

epistemic.reason: The support record explicitly supplies the 18:82 relational reading, but the candidate is legacy_unbound and lacks a complete typed trace for that contextual return.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Herkesçe arzu edilen ve kötülüğün karşısında duran genel olumlu değeri bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The x-y-r carrier presents good as a beneficial quality rather than a visible stockpile.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The garden-loss connections establish the failure of visible support, while the attributed 18:82 pointer supplies benefit reaching children through parental soundness.
branch_activations.activation: The good-value facet is activated as relational benefit that can persist beyond the lifespan of an asset.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Good can travel through a sound relation across time even when wealth cannot guarantee a result.
branch_activations.boundary: The reading does not condemn ordinary family or wealth, and it does not treat the legacy 18:82 pointer as an independently verified focus branch.

findings.title: Good as the surviving residue after display
findings.claim: What remains after visible display loses its supports can be perceived as the durable residue that enters the final account.
findings.mechanism: The two b-q-y facets distinguish persistence from the portion left behind, while the wide-context supports connect garden loss, windblown vegetation, and individually retained deeds.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader gets a concrete image for why the focus pairs transient adornment with lasting good: the latter is what survives successive losses.
findings.containment: The surviving residue is an attributed contextual reading, not a claim that every good deed is literally a detachable remainder or that the packet independently verifies the whole final-account mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The wide-context records supply the residue synthesis and its 18:49 retrospective duplicate, but they are legacy_unbound and do not provide a complete independent trace for every contextual step.

findings.title: Reward as returned recompense
findings.claim: The focus's thawab can be perceived as the recompense that returns an act to its doer, while the paired better comparison keeps reward and final outcome linked without making them identical.
findings.mechanism: The thawab carrier is activated by the local conclusion in 18:44 and the near-verbatim parallel in 19:76, where better reward is paired with a better final return.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear reward as a returned consequence of action rather than as decorative approval detached from what was done.
findings.containment: The branch allows good or bad recompense; this finding selects the positive focus context without claiming that reward and final destination are the same concept.

epistemic.reason: The activation is independently supported by two explicit connection records, but the packet does not supply a full morphological analysis of every target occurrence.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Yapılan iş, işi yapan kişiye iyi ya da kötü bir karşılık doğurur.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 18:44 and 19:76 pair better reward with a better outcome or final return in the Lord's presence.
branch_activations.activation: The recompense facet is activated as the good act's returned result.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Reward is part of the focus's return structure, not a free-floating compliment.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not collapse thawab into uqba or assert that every use of the root has the same positive polarity.

findings.title: Better as a comparative standard

findings.mechanism: The x-y-r selection facet is carried by both focus occurrences and triggered by the paired reward and final-return parallels in 18:44 and 19:76.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can track the focus's comparison as a judgment of alternatives rather than as an isolated praise word.
findings.containment: The finding concerns the comparative operation in this focus and does not claim that every x-y-r use expresses a final eschatological ranking.

epistemic.reason: The exact branch facet and two direct comparative parallels support the reading, while the packet leaves target morphology implicit.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Olasılıklar arasından daha iyi görüleni arayıp ayırmayı, seçmeyi ve seçilmiş sonucu bildirir.

branch_activations.activation: The selection facet is activated as the focus's criterion for choosing the better alternative.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus asks the reader to choose a lasting value, not merely to notice that it is pleasant or useful.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not make the focus a command to reject every near-term benefit or equate all comparisons with legal choice.

findings.title: Wealth reaching for continuity
findings.claim: The focus's mal can resonate as a claim that present wealth is asked to secure continuity, extending visible possession into an imagined guarantee across time.
findings.mechanism: The wealth carrier is activated by the counted possessions of 104:2 and the explicit permanence illusion in 104:3.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why visible accumulation is vulnerable to becoming a false promise of permanence.
findings.containment: The reading concerns the temptation to treat possession as continuity; it does not assert that every mention of wealth contains an immortality claim.

epistemic.reason: The two target connections directly support the permanence contrast, but the packet provides no direct target morphology and one derived connection has no separate evidence row.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: varlık; edinme, çoğalma ve başkasına kazandırma
branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişinin sahip olduğu ve değer taşıyan varlıkların bütünü bu dalın ad çekirdeğini oluşturur.
branch_activations.carrier: The mal carrier names visible, valued possession as the object under evaluation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 104:2 depicts counting wealth, while 104:3 states the corresponding illusion that wealth grants permanence.
branch_activations.activation: The possession facet is activated when wealth is extended from present ownership into imagined continuity.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Worldly wealth can become a failed attempt to make adornment endure by accumulation alone.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not say that ownership itself is the illusion or that all wealth-seeking has this intent.

findings.title: Adornment as a test of action
findings.claim: The focus's zina can be perceived as a visible class of worldly adornment whose presence tests what kind of action it elicits, while the adornment itself remains real and not categorically forbidden.
findings.mechanism: The worldly-adornment facet is carried by the focus and activated by the direct local parallel in 18:7 and the warning against extending one's gaze toward worldly splendor in 20:131.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold together the reality of beauty and the question of what people do with it, without turning the focus into a blanket ban on adornment.
findings.containment: The finding is about adornment as a testing field and evaluative contrast; it does not treat every adornment as blameworthy or erase the packet's qualifying adornment evidence.

epistemic.reason: A direct same-surah connection and a close warning about worldly splendor support the reading, while the packet does not provide a full target morphological trace.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: bezenmeye yarayan nitelik ve şeylerin bütünü
branch_activations.facet_statement: Dünyalık tür, malı, eşyayı ve toplumsal saygınlığı kişiyi bezeyen dışsal unsurlar olarak bir araya getirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The zina carrier gathers worldly goods and status as external elements that make a person appear adorned.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 18:7 makes earthly things an adornment and test of deeds, while 20:131 contrasts worldly splendor with the Lord's better enduring provision.
branch_activations.activation: The worldly-adornment facet is activated as the visible field in which action is tested and comparison is made.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Adornment is real but provisional, and its evaluative importance lies in what it discloses about action and attachment.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is about external adornment and does not absorb inner beauty, beautifying action, or a categorical prohibition.

findings.title: Worldly life as a growth-to-fragmentation phase
findings.claim: The focus's worldly life can be perceived as a living, productive phase whose visible abundance is vulnerable to dispersal, so the contrast carries a growth-to-fragmentation movement.
findings.mechanism: The life carrier's rain-fed growth facet is activated by the 10:24 parallel and the ordered 18:45 vegetation image immediately before the focus.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the temporal movement in the comparison: visible flourishing is a phase, not the final form of value.
findings.containment: This is a contextual analogy about transience and does not claim that the focus's life word itself means vegetation or that the entire rain parable is reproduced here.

epistemic.reason: The 10:24 connection is a close contextual parallel and 18:45 is an ordered local precursor, but the packet supplies no direct target morphology for the activation.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yağmurla gelen toprak canlılığı ve bolluk
branch_activations.facet_statement: Verimli toprak ile taze ve hareketli bitki, yağmurun yaşatıcı etkisinin görünür sonuçlarıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The al-hayat carrier presents worldly life as the visible phase of growth and abundance.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 10:24 turns rain-fed worldly growth into stubble, and the ordered 18:45 context supplies the local windblown-fragment image.
branch_activations.activation: The growth facet is activated as the first phase in the focus's contrast with what remains.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Worldly life can flourish visibly while remaining exposed to rapid dispersal.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation is analogical and does not redefine life as plant growth or import every detail of the rain parable.

findings.title: Remainder as communal soundness
findings.claim: The plural remainder can also carry the image of good or soundness left in a community after corruption is resisted, so what remains is not only an individual residue but a communal capacity that can oppose فساد.
findings.mechanism: The b-q-y residue facet is activated by the derived 11:86 and 11:116 connections, where what remains is set against corrupt accumulation and linked to people of discernment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can extend the focus's remainder image from private action to the good capacity that a community preserves.
findings.containment: This is an extension of the residue facet, not a claim that the focus directly addresses a named community or that every b-q-y form means communal soundness.

epistemic.reason: The two target references support the extension at root level, but both connection records are derived and the packet does not provide a direct target-evidence row for this activation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir topluluktan geriye kalan kişiler veya o toplulukta hâlâ bulunan iyilik ve sağlamlık payı da bu anlamla anlatılabilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The b-q-y carrier can name the good portion or sound people left after corruption's pressure.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The 11:86 and 11:116 rows contrast enduring remainder with corrupt accumulation and identify a preserving community capacity.
branch_activations.activation: The communal extension is activated when remainder means preserved goodness rather than only an amount left over.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: What remains can be a community's surviving soundness and resistance to corruption.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus remains an individual-facing comparison in its immediate wording; the communal sense is an exploratory root-level extension.

findings.title: Hope oriented toward a good return
findings.claim: The focus's amal can be perceived as expectation of a good return anchored in lasting work, rather than bare duration or undirected wish.
findings.mechanism: The hope carrier is activated by the focus's paired reward language and by the 18:44 and 19:76 parallels, where the better outcome is explicitly related to return.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can understand hope as directed expectation grounded in a better result, not as optimism detached from action.
findings.containment: The finding does not specify a single promised outcome and does not import the rejected HFT proposal that merciful delay is necessarily a formative interval.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and two explicit reward-return parallels support the direction of hope, while the packet does not supply a more specific target morphology or outcome mapping.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Hope is the forward-facing counterpart to the focus's claim that good work is better in reward and outcome.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch remains hope and waiting for good; it does not become proof of a detailed timetable or a specific emotional state.

findings.title: The Lord's side as evaluative relation
findings.claim: The phrase at the Lord's side can be perceived as an evaluative and governing relation: better reward and hope are held within the Lord's measure, not an impersonal scale.
findings.mechanism: The near-presence/evaluation carrier and the ownership-governance carrier are activated by parallels that place what is better and enduring with God.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the comparison as accountable to a personal divine standard rather than as a free-floating ranking of outcomes.
findings.containment: The finding uses relational and governance facets without turning near the Lord into a spatial claim or treating the human use of ownership language as absolute lordship.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and three explicit with-God comparison rows support the evaluative relation, but the packet does not provide a complete target morphological analysis.

findings.title: Lasting good as sound action
findings.claim: The salihat carrier can be perceived as sound, repaired, beneficial action, so the lasting alternative is defined by deed quality rather than persistence alone.
findings.mechanism: The salih facet is activated by explicit rows stating that the reward of good-doers is not lost, that God's reward is better, and that righteousness is more than outward display.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can avoid reducing the focus's lasting works to mere endurance; what lasts must also be good and sound.
findings.containment: The finding stays with the good-and-sound action facet and does not claim that every form of repair or every use of the root is present in the focus.

epistemic.reason: Three explicit connection records support the action-quality reading, while the packet does not supply a complete target morphology for all three parallels.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi, iş veya şey bozukluğun ve kötülüğün karşıtı olan iyi, düzgün ve yararlı bir durumda bulunur.
branch_activations.carrier: The salihat carrier names deeds that are good, sound, and beneficial rather than merely extant.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 18:30 preserves the reward of good-doers, 28:80 calls God's reward better for those who do good, and 2:177 defines righteousness beyond outward display.
branch_activations.activation: The good-and-sound facet is activated as the quality condition on the works that the focus calls lasting.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The lasting alternative is durable good action, not bare persistence detached from moral quality.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not import every specialized or causative sense of the root into the focus.
